requirements.expectation: Each Human principal is ensured through the station ensure-human leg, mints a one-time register token from the station, registers its disposable Bot with that token, and onboards it with the testing domain, review skill and local scope; the owner alone marks its Bot public afterwards. All bootstrap and visibility legs carry per-request mock admission on the station face only; the ownership ledger records the two Bot uuid/owner pairs.

The manager creates a normal Group driven by its registered driver Bot, narrows the Group to private visibility, and opens exactly one Session titled for session-only participation; creation acknowledges 201 and the Group and Session ids join the ownership journal.

Before any invitation the owner is refused Group reads with 403 forbidden; once the manager adds the owned Bot as a Session-only participant the owner reads the Group while its participant projection still hides the Session-only Bot; the stranger Human stays refused.

The owner flips its own Bot Session mode between muted and auto with exact echo and read-back; patching the manager driver Bot, selecting an invalid bot mode, widening the message view scope to full as non-manager, or selecting an invalid message view scope is refused with forbidden, invalid_participant_mode, message_view_scope_forbidden or invalid_message_view_scope and no denied patch partially writes.

The owner cannot retitle or delete the manager Session, rename or delete the manager Group, invite the driver Bot into the Session, or patch a participant that never existed: foreign Session and Group mutations and the foreign invite answer forbidden, the manager missing-target read answers participant_not_found while the owner missing-target read answers forbidden.

A Human self-joins only through its owned active Bot: the owner Human joins present with full view scope by exact echo, bot modes and manager-absent writes are refused, a stranger cannot self-add or widen its scope, the manager may narrow the Human scope to participant, and the loopback pairs (participant/absent, full/present) echo and read back exactly.

Session listing scoped by view_bot_id answers 200 only for a Bot the requester owns and forbidden for the manager driver Bot; message history reads, collect add and collect remove succeed for the participating owner while collect add answers forbidden for the stranger.

Manager revocation of the owned Bot leaves the Human relation intact and the owner keeps Group reads while Bot-mode patches are refused; revoking the Human relation too denies the owner both Group and Session reads while the manager retains its Group read.

Teardown deletes the Session and the Group through the manager public face and both owned Bots through their station owners; every disposition failure fails the whole story instead of leaking owned state.
